advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard _ce_spend_today against a present-but-empty Total/UnblendedCost entry (use .get chains and default to 0.0) so a malformed period does not raise KeyError and abort the tick.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:354: `    results = resp.get("ResultsByTime", [])`
infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:357: `    return float(results[0]["Total"]["UnblendedCost"]["Amount"])`
Caller only guards ClientError: handler.py:500 `except ClientError as exc:` — a KeyError escapes and aborts the tick
Ticket comment explicitly lists this as unactioned: '_ce_spend_today still assumes a present Total object when results exist.'
advisory.finding: _ce_spend_today indexes results[0]['Total']['UnblendedCost']['Amount'] whenever ResultsByTime is non-empty, but Cost Explorer returns a period entry with an empty/absent Total for periods with no data; that raises KeyError, which is NOT a ClientError, so the caller's `except ClientError` does not catch it and the whole handler tick aborts — disabling enforcement, release, and state persistence.
scenarios: A UTC day whose CE result period has no cost data yet returns an entry with an empty Total dict
Any CE response shape variation where UnblendedCost is absent
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the final line with defensive gets: `total = results[0].get("Total", {}).get("UnblendedCost", {}).get("Amount"); return float(total) if total is not None else 0.0`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider whether `metered is None` should bypass CE rate limiting on every tick, or still honor last_poll/CE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS during a sustained metered outage.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:493: `    if due or metered is None or metered * 5 >= THRESHOLD_USD * 4:`
Module docstring: 'CE is therefore polled at most once per CE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default hourly)'
A sustained CloudWatch outage keeps metered None on every tick, so CE is hit every 5 minutes regardless of last_poll
advisory.finding: During a CloudWatch/metered outage (metered is None), the CE poll gate `if due or metered is None or ...` forces a Cost Explorer call on every 5-minute tick, defeating the CE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS rate limiting exactly when the outage may persist for hours — the very per-request charges the design set out to avoid.
scenarios: Prolonged CloudWatch ListMetrics/GetMetricData outage while CE stays healthy

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In DRY_RUN, suppress or clearly label the release/trip SNS notifications so they cannot claim an action that did not occur.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:428: `    if DRY_RUN:` (in _apply) returns empty touched without acting
handler.py:563: `        touched = _apply(attach=False)` then handler.py:564 `        _notify("Bedrock daily cap released", ...)`
handler.py:568: `+ "\n  ".join(touched or ["(nothing — see logs)"])`
advisory.finding: When DRY_RUN is set and a release would occur, _apply(attach=False) is a no-op returning [], yet the handler's returned deny_attached calls _is_attached() which re-reads live IAM and reports True — while the 'Bedrock daily cap released' SNS notification is still published, claiming detachment that did not happen.
scenarios: Operator sets DRY_RUN=true to lift the cap for a day while a deny is attached and spend drops under threshold

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the log-group / SSM-state ARN region and the ce/cloudwatch client region from var.aws_region (or data.aws_region.current) instead of the hardcoded "us-east-1", or document that this stack is us-east-1-only and add a validation guard.
evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf:295-299 `Resource = format("arn:aws:logs:%s:%s:log-group:/aws/lambda/%s:*", "us-east-1", ...)`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:317-322 `format("arn:aws:ssm:%s:%s:parameter/%s/state", "us-east-1", ...)`
main.tf:5-7 `provider "aws" { region = var.aws_region }`
variables.tf:1-5 `variable "aws_region" { ... default = "us-east-1" }`
The aws_cloudwatch_log_group and aws_lambda_function set no region override, so they inherit var.aws_region while the IAM ARNs are pinned to a literal us-east-1.
advisory.finding: The Lambda's IAM policy hardcodes region "us-east-1" in the Logs and State ARNs (and the handler hardcodes region_name="us-east-1" for the ce client), but the AWS provider deploys the Lambda, log group, and SSM parameter into var.aws_region (default us-east-1). If var.aws_region is overridden to any non-us-east-1 region, the Lambda and its log group are created in that region while the IAM grant references log-group and parameter ARNs in us-east-1, so logging (logs:CreateLogGroup/PutLogEvents) and SSM state read/write are denied, and enforcement silently stops.
scenarios: Deploying this stack in a region other than us-east-1 by setting var.aws_region
A future refactor that parameterizes the region for reuse in another account/region
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the literal "us-east-1" in the Logs and State ARN format() calls with var.aws_region (or data.aws_region.current.name), and align the handler's REGIONS/ce region with the same source.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give aws_budgets_budget.bedrock_daily a stable name independent of the cap value (e.g. "bedrock-daily") so changing the cap is an in-place update, not a replace.
evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf:215 `name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf:217 `limit_amount = tostring(var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)` already carries the cap value, so encoding it in the name too couples the immutable name to a routinely-tuned input.
README.md guidance: "**Change the cap:** set `bedrock_daily_cap_usd` and apply." — the documented normal operation triggers a destroy/recreate of the alerting budget.
advisory.finding: The DAILY budget resource name embeds the cap dollar value: name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd). aws_budgets_budget.name is immutable, so changing bedrock_daily_cap_usd forces Terraform to destroy and recreate the budget rather than update it in place. On a live cost-control tripwire this deletes the existing budget (and its notification history) and briefly leaves no alerting budget during the replace.
scenarios: Operator raises or lowers bedrock_daily_cap_usd and runs terraform apply as the README instructs
advisory.suggested_fix: Change name to a constant like format("bedrock-daily") or "bedrock-daily-cap"; keep the dollar value only in limit_amount.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that a fresh cap trip publishes an SNS message with subject beginning 'Bedrock daily cap TRIPPED'.
evidence: handler.py adds the trip notify branch: `_notify(f"Bedrock daily cap TRIPPED — {spend:,.2f} >= {THRESHOLD_USD:,.2f}", ...)` guarded by `if first_trip:`

test_trip_records_day_and_attaches_every_target (lines 265-273) asserts only `result["deny_attached"] is True`, `tripped_day`, and `assert_policy_attached(...)` — no assertion on `fake_aws.sns.published`
search for `TRIPPED` in the test file returns (no matches); only the WARNING subject is asserted at line 564
advisory.finding: The first-trip TRIPPED SNS notification is newly added behavior but no test asserts it is published; test_trip_records_day_and_attaches_every_target drives a fresh trip (THRESHOLD + len("x"), no prior attachment) and asserts state/attachment only, so a regression removing the _notify("Bedrock daily cap TRIPPED"...) call would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor or edit drops/short-circuits the TRIPPED _notify call; operators stop receiving the hard-cap alert but all tests still pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_trip_records_day_and_attaches_every_target, assert `[m["Subject"] for m in fake_aws.sns.published]` contains a subject starting with 'Bedrock daily cap TRIPPED'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that the release path publishes an SNS message with subject 'Bedrock daily cap released'.
evidence: handler.py adds the release notify branch: `_notify("Bedrock daily cap released", ...)` under `if any_attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and not signal_unavailable:`

test_releases_on_later_utc_day_when_spend_is_back_under (lines 276-287) asserts only `result["deny_attached"] is False` and `assert_policy_attached(fake_aws, attached=False)` — no assertion on `fake_aws.sns.published`
search for `released` in the test file returns (no matches)
advisory.finding: The cap-release SNS notification is newly added behavior but no test asserts it is published; test_releases_on_later_utc_day_when_spend_is_back_under drives the release path (prior full attachment, spend under threshold) and asserts detachment only, so a regression removing the _notify("Bedrock daily cap released"...) call would go undetected.
scenarios: A change drops the release _notify call; the deny still detaches but no 'released' alert is sent, and every test remains green.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_releases_on_later_utc_day_when_spend_is_back_under, assert `fake_aws.sns.published` contains a message with subject 'Bedrock daily cap released'.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'metric listing succeeded but no usage' (return 0.0) from 'listing/backend failed' (return None) in _metered_spend so a zero-usage day is not misread as unavailable.
evidence: infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:338: `    if not found_series:`
infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py:340: `        return None`
found_series is only set True when at least one per-ModelId token series exists, so genuine zero-usage yields the same None as a backend outage
handler.py:562: `    if any_attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and not signal_unavailable:` — release is gated by signal availability
Ticket comment lists it unactioned: '_metered_spend still cannot distinguish genuinely zero usage from missing per-model series.'
blocking.finding: _metered_spend returns None (interpreted as 'unavailable') both when the CloudWatch listing genuinely found no per-model Bedrock series (a quiet day with zero usage) and when the metric backend produced nothing — the two worlds are indistinguishable. Because signal_unavailable then blocks the release branch (line 562), a legitimately zero-usage day cannot release an existing deny via the metered signal, and enforcement leans on CE alone.
scenarios: A UTC day with no Bedrock invocations at all
A region that has never emitted AWS/Bedrock metrics (e.g. us-west-2 per the tf comment) contributing no series

handler.py fail-closed design: unpriced models are priced at UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K "set deliberately HIGH", so a mis-normalised/unpinned model id can over-estimate spend and trip the cap early, taking Admin's Bedrock access with it.
dropped.finding: The deny-policy enforcement targets include the IAM group "Admin" by default (bedrock_cap_target_groups default = ["Admin"]). When the cap trips, an explicit Deny for Bedrock invocation actions is attached to the Admin group, which is a very large blast radius: any breach (including a false trip driven by the deliberately-high UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K fail-closed pricing) instantly blocks all Bedrock invocation for every admin principal account-wide.
scenarios: A new or renamed Bedrock model id fails to normalise/match a rate and is priced at the fail-closed fallback, over-estimating spend and tripping the cap
Cost Explorer/CloudWatch signal skew causes an early trip
